findings.title: Contradictory duplicate JSON object members are silently discarded before validation
findings.observed: 25 separate uncached CLI processes return PASS/exit 0 despite contradictory repeated members; the correct authoritative value appears last.
findings.expected: Reject duplicate receipt object members before parsed-field validation and return FAIL/nonzero.
findings.mechanism: json.loads uses last-member-wins parsing. Field-set, row-uniqueness, strict type and source-value checks operate on a dict after earlier contradictory declarations have disappeared.
findings.impact: E-02 fail-closed receipt contract is not met. The probes preserve actual pinned Git and installed build bytes; this is acceptance of contradictory declarations, not proof of arbitrary source replacement or a runtime vulnerability.
findings.correctionRequest: Assigned maker should reject repeated JSON object member names at all nesting levels in receipt/parser entry points and add raw-byte uncached CLI regressions for contradictory and same-value duplicates. Apply the policy consistently to source-binding, candidate provenance, predecessor outputs, installed package identity and shared JSON loaders. Preserve exact source pins and current passing controls. Auditor makes no candidate edits.
findings.limitations: Finite sampled duplicate keys; shared parser inspection indicates broader exposure but no exhaustive proof for every key. logged_json_value at line 170 was inspected only; no mutation of pinned historical log blobs or manifests was attempted.
